name: DERDA
description: Derda is a two-player Jass game that was once popular in Poland, particularly among currency traders, gamblers, and the underworld during the communist era. It is closely related to Clobyosh and features unique bidding mechanics and bonus scoring for sequences and special cards.

content.text: Derda is a two-player Jass game that was once popular in Poland, particularly among currency traders, gamblers, and the underworld during the communist era. It is closely related to Clobyosh and features unique bidding mechanics and bonus scoring for sequences and special cards.

Country/Region of Origin: Poland
Time Period: Peak popularity during communist era (1945-1989)
Historical Development: First played in Łódź and Warsaw, spread throughout Poland by 1960
Cultural Significance: Associated with cinkciarze (illicit currency traders), gamblers, and underworld figures; featured in the 1997 movie 'Sztos'

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 2
Optimal Players: 2
Partnerships: None - individual head-to-head play

Type: 32-card French suited pack
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Cards used: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit

32-card French suited pack
Score slate and chalk for special notation
Table space for cards and talon

First deal: 6 cards to each player in packets of 3
Turn-up card: 13th card suggests trump
Second deal (if trumps chosen): 3 more cards to each player
Remaining 13 cards form talon with top card face up

items.text: Different target score: Players may agree a lower or higher target than 500 for a shorter or longer game.
